txt: After a while, he cranes his head side-to-side and sighs: "Fucking loincloths really did him in."
Another grunt. He's turned his attention to the gates and seems tense.
He abruptly changes the subject: "Let's talk about our right to work."
He ignores your question, choosing instead to turn to the emaciated workers -- raising both fists in the air. The clothes are obviously not his.
He looks annoyed. "Things are busy enough. You going to waste less of my time?"
He nods. "You go take the bastards down a peg or two. Squeeze them a little. Show them the rule of law." He bellows at the gates: "LET US WORK!"
He nods. "You go, take the bastards down a peg or two. Squeeze them a little. Show them the rule of law." He bellows at the gates: "LET US WORK!"
He pauses, then abruptly changes the subject: "Let's talk about our right to work."
He smirks. "Not before you get in there and get your ass whooped. Learn by failure, I always say."
He squints at you --  a little spark of violence gutters in his eyes. Then he blinks and turns to his men. "We're done here. I have a strike to break."
Silence. He takes the photo. Grey eyes dart  back and forth on the glossy surface -- his face is unmoving.
Suddenly the laughter stops. "Drowned in a creek a week later. Spirits my ass."
The beefy man snorts and spits on the ground. "They know me -- that's bullshit." He turns his attention back to the harbour gates.
The beefy man snorts and spits on the ground. "Yeah. I don't know either." He turns his attention back to the harbour gates.
The burly man has a set of not-very-sweet-nor-impressive boots protruding out from under the baggy, hanging folds. They are of little interest to you.
The hulking man oozes stark scepticism.
The man has turned his attention elsewhere, he shakes his fist slowly -- while observing you from the corner of his eye.
The man turns to look behind him -- at the behemoth appearing around the corner, approaching him, walking past him...
The man's breathing steadies but his eyes are still narrow. Slowly he's trying to get his 'Right to Work' dance back on...
The physically impressive man-tower has turned his attention back to the gates. He ignores your presence.
Wordless, he takes the photo and looks at it. Grey eyes dart back and forth on the glossy surface -- his face is unmoving.
"Am I a suspect?" His eyes narrow. "Done no crimes. I only fight for the rights of people."
"And I don't mean the scrawny Mesque punk either." He points at the dockworker idling on the staircase. "I mean Head-Measurer -- or whatever he is."
"Around." He shifts his gaze away. "Eminent Domain. Previous... workplace."
"At dawn he comes upon two kipts, breeding in the bushes by the river. Or maybe they weren't breeding -- maybe they were just making eyes at each other. I like to think they were breeding..."
"Bad." The man glares at you. "Standing on a narrow bridge, he's got a strategically advantageous position. And he's trained."
"Basteeerds! We have a RIGHT TO WORK!" the man yells towards the harbour gates. His voice is the loudest of the lot -- and oddly screechy for a man his size.
"Beats me. They mumble nonsense about *board rooms* and *workers' rights*. While we --" he raises his fist and starts shouting again, "-- HAVE THE RIGHT TO WORK!"
"Besides, we're not that different." He leans closer. "It helps if people see us talking -- cops and strikebreakers together. Shows authorities are on our side. Builds confidence."
"Big mess. Caused by Union greed." He shoots you a wary, distrustful look. "But I only fight for the rights of people."
"Don't think so," he grunts, barely glancing at it.
"Don't think so," he grunts.
"Establishment hasn't had its fill, is that right? First they obstruct our work, then they come for our shoes."
"FREE FLOW OF COMMERCE!" The man yells and wipes his face. Sweat is dripping down his brow.
"Fucking bug..." He breathes out slowly -- his giant chest deflating and his mouth slightly open.
"Fucking loincloth..." He stares you down mutely for a second.
"Fucking mask is getting sweaty. I want take my mask off, but..." He shrugs.
"Go ahead." He turns toward the gate, slowly, and yells: "All right now. FREE COMMERCE! KEEP THE GOODS FLOWING!"
"God..." He suddenly bursts out laughing. "Mason couldn't let go. Cut the tits off her cold body and fuckin' ate them. Said primitive spirits were watching over him now..."
"Good choice." He nods.
"Good. We're fighting for a cause here." He chants at the gates: "RIGHT TO WORK! RIGHT TO WORK!"
"Hah! Couldn't handle us. A cause gives the workers strength. Gives them power." He bellows at the gates: "We have -- A RIGHT TO WORK!"
"Have fun." He snorts. "Union shits are on full strike. Don't think they're going to let you through the gates. You trying to meet their fat boss?"

"He's spent a month behind enemy lines scouting kipt villages. Nothing but fucking bugs and snakes for fun. Men are getting restless... there's talk of switching *employers*..." He licks his lips, as if drunk suddenly.
"Hell no. I'm just an honest scab. I won't have talk like that around here, you understand?"
"Hold up and stay frosty, everyone! Cops are here." The broad-shouldered alpha male turns to you. He's a full head taller than everybody else here.
"Honest men and women. With rights -- to work. To be useful. Not toys for corporate interests." The man runs a hand through his steadily graying military haircut.
"How about you fuck off now, huh?"
"Huge Semenese guy standing up there on the overhead passage. Won't let anyone by. The access panel is right behind him."
"I can tell you what this one means. Only one." He squints at it. It's so small. "You wanna hear what happened here?"
"I don't know how the Union has a trained killer up there, but that one's no joke. And my men are tired. And hungry. They're WORKERS, not fighters."
"I don't trust cops, but... I can see you understand the --" He raises his voice and chants: "RIGHT TO WORK! RIGHT TO WORK!"
"I know nothing about a murder." His reply is snappy and terse.
"I work hard." His voice booms ever louder: "And I would work *even harder* -- if the fuckers would LET US WORK!"
"It's just... nature. This guy," he points at the picture, "he used to say evil is when nature and spirit meet in the wrong place."
"LET US THROUGH, LOINCLOTHS!"
"LET US WORK!"
"Like civilized folk, you mean?" The man rubs his chin. "These native fucks don't understand *civilized*."
"Look alive back there! LET US WORK!!!"
"Look at you, RCM rent-a-cops!" A loud voice booms in from below: "Guarding that bridge like Evrart's lapdogs, is this where it's at now? The RCM is for sale?"

"Main gate's locked -- would take *heavy ordnance* to bust it open. Could try to get in through the secretary's office." He points up the stairs. "Door's locked. The guard's blocking the way to the access panel."
"Maybe you should ask *them* the questions, like why we're not allowed to make a living here?" He bellows to the gates: "SHAME ON YOU!"
"Might be time. Don't let the fat bastards tread on you. Cops tend to side with the higher-ups, but you're essentially still *workers*."
"Nah, you've earned it." He turns toward the gate, slowly, and yells: "All right now! FREE COMMERCE! KEEP THE GOODS FLOWING!"
"Nice aggression with the native." He nods in approval. "Don't let the chief fool you next time. You don't need to be that up in his face -- leave yourself space to move."
"No -- I was in the Domain. In Jamrock. Being a bouncer."
"No, don't think we've met before." His eyes narrow with mistrust. "I came to help out *the people*."
"No. I was somewhere else. That's just a *guess*. As to what this one little star on his belly might mean. I'm just a bouncer."
"No. They will give up eventually. Or get drunk. Leave the button unguarded. Then we charge." The man rubs his jaw -- a perfect, lightly bearded square wedge.
"No." He slowly shakes his head. "I'm not a fighter -- I'm a WORKER!"
"No."

"Our boy -- he's only a captain then -- but he knows how these men think. If they don't see action soon..." His voice gets strangely quiet. A long, long way from *right to work*. His gaze pierces the paper.
"Our colonel is *deep* in the bush here. Deep in the fucking bush, in Banaital, '41... Monsoon season. He's on a reconnaissance mission."
"Pity." He turns around and bellows at the gates: "LET US WORK!"
"RIGHT TO WORK! RIGHT TO WORK!" the ostensible leader of the strikebreakers chants furiously. "SHAME ON YOU!"
"RIGHT TO WORK! RIGHT TO WORK!"
"RIGHT TO WORK!!" the man chants, then turns to you. "Back again, eh? Here to show the militia's support for our cause?"

"RIGHT TO WORK!" He again shakes his large fist, then turns back to you. "It's shameful, cops doing nothing. You should bring backup, open the gates for us. Blockading gainful employment for workers is a *crime*."
"RIGHT TO WORK!" He seems to have returned to his previous routine, as if he'd never seen the photo of the tattoo.
"Rights of people. Rights of workers. To have gainful employment. To make a salary and feed their families."

"She was quite the entertainment. For the week she lasted. Expired in the hands of Sarge Mason -- the kinda guy who'd make Chief there," he nods towards the man on the gates, "shit his pants and cry like a bitch."
"So anyway, cop. That's where I'm from. It would be *stupid* to doubt that."
"That's what they always say, before stabbing you in the back. You want boots? Go find your own."
"Uh huh. Was a long time ago." The man is quickly losing interest in talking with you.
"Unexpected situation. But we hold the pressure on, until someone makes a mistake. Then it's our time, we strike." The man rubs his jaw -- a lightly bearded square wedge.
"WE'RE NOT GOING ANYWHERE!"
"Wait. They might go home eventually. Or get drunk. Leave the access panel unguarded. Or the company sends someone to reason with them..."
"We came here to help the harbour run smoothly in time of crisis. If Union fucks don't want work, they ought let in those *WHO DO WANT WORK*."
"We have families to feed, you piece of shit!" He points his finger at the man sitting on the railing.
"We shot the boy, he was useless, but the girl... she was nice. A little fat you know. But not too old."
"We were promised work." He points to the gates. "We'd be in there -- WORKING -- if the bastards hadn't shut the gates."
"We're all workers. Right? Workers stick together. Came from the Eminent Domain, in Jamrock. Background's in odd-jobs -- heavy lifting, cargo hauling, bouncer work. I know the drill."
"We're here to fight for a cause. Stripes usually have problems with people who have *causes*."
"Went native on the chief, huh?" He nods in approval. "Those ballerina antics were reckless. Should have just punched him in the throat again."
"What are you talking about? I'm not tense."
"What it *means*...." He points to one tiny star in the web of lines, away from the man's heart, almost on his stomach.
"What's it to you?" Deep-set suspicion drips from every syllable.
"What's the matter, militiaman... no stomach for it?" He looks at the photo in your hand and smiles. "This man was worth a thousand loincloths. We're done talking here."
"When a bunch of ungrateful, lazy cockroaches can't get their act together. Decide to block honest work for other people." He shifts uncomfortably in his worker's overalls.
"Why don't *you* go arrest them instead? I'm sure they've done plenty of criminal shit, they have *that look*."
"Worked at... *Territorial*. Ring a bell?"
"Workers rights! WORKERS RIGHTS!"
"Wouldn't put it past these harbour bugs. They'd do *anything* to stay alive."
"Yeah, I saw your ballerina moves up there." The man spits out a yellow clot. "In a real fight these acrobatics will get you killed faster than a bullet."
"Yeah."
"Yeah?" The man grunts. "What makes you say that?"
"You bet it was."
"You caught him off guard -- that only happens once. Now he's alert, standing on a narrow bridge and *my* men are tired and hungry..."
"You do that."
"You here to fuck with us? Beat the honest worker down?"
"You think they follow because I'm big and loud? No, they follow the rules of the market. The rules of the economy. Because they were --" he starts bellowing, "-- GIVEN A JOB TO DO."
"Your gut's got too much alcohol in it. Getting delirious." The bulky man guffaws and turns away from you, focusing again on the harbour gates.
